first_3_seconds: Phone sits on a gas station counter as the cashier's view. A big man in a red shirt and belt buckle struts up to the register asking for five on diesel, and a hard hat in a hi-vis vest steps in behind him.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "When a trade worker runs into a trucker". Spoken: "What's up, Joe? ... You doing 1,800 miles today?"
why_it_went_viral: 56x the account median and the only one of his top ten with a real share rate (0.78 percent, about 10x his other hits). It picks a fight between two tribes ("trucking ain't a trade") so both sides send it and argue in the comments, and 63 seconds of escalating insults (clean vest, soft hands) keeps them watching.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Truckers to the union or trades buddy who talks down on driving, and trades guys back to their trucker friends
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: State one side of an old truck-world argument straight to the camera as if the viewer just said the other side, and escalate the insults for 30 seconds.

first_3_seconds: Cashier point of view. A man in a grey Carhartt tee sets a foam box and a stack of sauce cups on the counter and opens the box to show one piece of chicken.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Customers when you charge for sauce". Spoken: "Hey, man, I just got one piece of chicken. That's it. $1.29."
why_it_went_viral: 32x median on views but only 0.04 percent shares, so this is watch-time and comment fuel, not send fuel. Everyone has been charged for sauce, and the customer's rising outrage ("Chick-fil-A says my pleasure") plays as a one-take argument people watch to the end.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Mostly not shared. A few send it to the friend who hoards sauce or fights every small charge
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Play one stubborn customer arguing a tiny charge to an unseen clerk, camera set where the clerk would stand.

first_3_seconds: Cashier point of view. Man in a dark Carhartt tee puts a big foam box on the counter and keeps his hand flat on the lid.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "When the customer lies about their order". Spoken: "I just got a one-piece chicken tender and a piece of white toast."
why_it_went_viral: 28x median. The hand on the lid sets up a reveal in the first two seconds, so viewers stay 40 seconds to see the box opened (six pieces, then he blames the cook). Shares are low (0.07 percent), it is a retention piece.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Gas station and food counter workers to coworkers, "this is every day"
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Open with a closed box or covered thing you refuse to open, stall with excuses, then show it and blame someone else.

first_3_seconds: Cashier point of view. Same man sets two stacked foam boxes on the counter and says it is just toast and fries.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "How customers lie about their order". Spoken: "I got just a piece of toast and an order of fries in there."
why_it_went_viral: 27x median. It is the same closed-box reveal as his number 3 hit run again four months later, which shows the format is the engine, not the single joke. 0.05 percent shares, so watch time carried it.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Counter and restaurant workers to coworkers
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Repeat a proven bit with one detail changed (bigger box, bigger lie) and treat it as a series.

first_3_seconds: Cashier point of view. Man in a dark long sleeve walks up holding a foam cup, sets it on the counter and points at the camera.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Regulars when they see a new cashier". Spoken: "How you doing, sir. So buddy, new here?"
why_it_went_viral: 24x median. The entitled 15-year regular who has "never paid for a pop" is a character every small-town store and shop knows, and he lectures the new kid for a full minute. 0.04 percent shares, strong completion.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Small-town clerks and counter guys to coworkers, "this is so-and-so"
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Play the regular who expects the old deal and lectures the new guy, spoken straight to the lens.

first_3_seconds: Phone on a dispatch desk. A dispatcher types at two monitors showing a load map while two truckers in company shirts lean on the counter.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "POV- Truckers negotiating loads". Spoken: "Every time I ring the bell add 500."
why_it_went_viral: 22x median with a slightly better share rate (0.12 percent) because it is inside-trucking humor: two drivers bidding miles against each other while the dispatcher gets squeezed. It needs three people and a real office, and the setting is doing a lot of the work.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Truckers to their dispatcher, and dispatchers to their drivers
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Not a solo shape as shot. The solo version is one man haggling a rate out loud with a voice on the phone.

first_3_seconds: Backyard patio. A pressure washer is spraying siding while the customer walks into the spray line waving his arms to stop him, then turns to the camera.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "When you tell the contractor you're paying cash". Spoken: "How much is it gonna be?" then "I'm gonna pay with cash."
why_it_went_viral: 21x median. One word (cash) flips the whole mood and the price, which every tradesman and every customer recognizes instantly. 0.12 percent shares, so recognition more than sending.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Contractors and side-work guys to each other, and customers to their handyman
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Show the before and after of one magic word: the quote in a normal voice, then the same quote after hearing cash.

first_3_seconds: Wide shot of a black Ram in a parking lot, then a cut to a man in a hard hat and hi-vis vest eating a hot dog in the driver's seat as someone walks up to his window.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "You can't get a trade worker off break". Spoken: "Jojo, hey, I need to cut your break a little short."
why_it_went_viral: 18x median and his best share rate among the non-trade-war skits (0.14 percent). Break time is sacred on every crew, and a man in a truck cab refusing to put the hot dog down even after being fired is the fantasy version of what they all want to say.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Crew guys to the group chat and to the foreman who interrupts lunch
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Sit in the truck cab mid-lunch, treat the camera as the boss at the window, and refuse to move.

first_3_seconds: Shot from behind a hot food case full of fried chicken. A man in a white tee walks up, points at the food and leans over the glass.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Customers that come in at closing for a deal". Spoken: "What time y'all close? ... You want to run a deal on that?"
why_it_went_viral: 16x median. The closing-time haggler is another character every counter worker knows, and the camera angle behind the food makes the viewer the clerk. Low shares (0.06 percent), carried by watch time and comments.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Food counter and convenience store workers to coworkers
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Play the guy who shows up at closing wanting a deal, camera placed behind the thing he is trying to get cheap.

first_3_seconds: Wide shot of a gas station aisle. A man in a grey tee dances toward the register waving a five dollar bill over his head, grinning.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Diesel customers at the gas station". Spoken: "You heard the big news, brother? ... Give me five on that diesel, but not that regular diesel. Give me that red dye."
why_it_went_viral: 15x median with his second best share rate (0.43 percent). It rides a diesel news rumor (the character claims red dye off-road fuel is legal now) and plays the guy who was running it anyway, so diesel owners send it as both a joke and a "did you hear this".
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Diesel truck owners to the buddy who runs or jokes about running red dye
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Walk in celebrating a piece of diesel news as a character who takes it one step too far, opening on movement instead of a standing start.

first_3_seconds: A monkey face cutout with eyes closed, slowly lifting its chin, pasted over a dark truck cab interior at night. White caption box sits above it the whole time.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "POV: leaving for work in the dark while everyone else is snug as a bug in a rug". Audio is a sad song lyric.
why_it_went_viral: 908x the account median and 3.51 percent shares on a 9 second clip. The dark truck cab before sunrise is a feeling every early-shift worker has had alone, and the sad music plus a proud, tired face says it without a word spoken.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Early-shift workers to their wife or girlfriend still in bed, and to the crew chat
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: One static shot of his own tired face in the dark cab before work, one line of text above, sad sound, under 10 seconds.

first_3_seconds: Macho Man Randy Savage cutout in a neon hat pulls off his sunglasses and leans bug-eyed into the lens, pasted over a jobsite photo.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "POV: that one coworker at 6:30am". Audio: "I'm jacked up on 10,000 milligrams of caffeine"
why_it_went_viral: 436x median and the highest share rate in this batch (4.73 percent). "That one coworker" is a tag-a-friend prompt in disguise: every crew has the guy on three energy drinks at dawn, so people send it straight to him.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Crew members to the wired morning coworker, or to the chat with his name
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: That one guy at [early hour] text over himself acting it out in the cab or lip-syncing a known wild sound clip.

first_3_seconds: Conor McGregor cutout struts toward the camera, arms swinging, over a photo of a house under construction. Two lines of text sit at the top.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "(Work starts at 7am) That one guy at 6:15:"
why_it_went_viral: 400x median but the lowest share rate of the account's top five (1.31 percent). Same "that one guy" early-bird idea as number 2 with a weaker clip, so it got views from the strut and fewer sends.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Crew members to the guy who always shows up 45 minutes early
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Two-line text setup (the rule, then "that one guy") over himself pulling in or walking up far too early.

first_3_seconds: A heavyset man in a white shirt and cap is mid-rant, lunging forward while a security guard holds him back, pasted over a jobsite photo.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "POV: the real you slips out at work after that one coworker says the wrong thing"
why_it_went_viral: 234x median, 3.76 percent shares. Holding your temper at work until one coworker pushes it is universal, and the clip is a full meltdown. The joke is about temper and not race, but the audio is a rant full of the n-word, so the sound itself is not something Jacob should reuse.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Workers to the coworker who pushes their buttons, or to a friend who knows about him
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: The real you slips out when... text over his own face going from calm to done, no borrowed audio.

first_3_seconds: John C. Reilly in a tuxedo from the Step Brothers job interview scene talks to the camera, cut with Will Ferrell, pasted over a construction site photo.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "POV: the kind of employees my company hires". Audio: "I am no good before 11 a.m."
why_it_went_viral: 222x median, 4.48 percent shares. It lets workers complain about the useless new hire without naming anyone, and the movie scene is already loved, so the text only has to aim it at work.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Workers to the crew chat about the new hire, and to the boss as a jab
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: A deadpan list of ridiculous limitations spoken to the camera as the worst new hire, under one line of text.

first_3_seconds: Jim Carrey and Jeff Daniels from Dumb and Dumber stand side by side on a gravel lot. Labels read Coworker and Me, and Me points off into the distance.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Boss: who wants to come in on Saturday?" with labels "Coworker:" and "Me:"
why_it_went_viral: 170x median, 4.33 percent shares in 8 seconds. Dodging Saturday work is shared by every hourly worker, and the Boss, Coworker, Me labels make the joke readable in one second with the sound off.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Workers to the coworker who always says yes to Saturday, and to the boss
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Boss line as text, then his own reaction shot labeled Me (pointing away, already leaving).

first_3_seconds: A young man in glasses and a black tee walks into frame in an unfinished drywall room, looks up at the ceiling and his jaw drops as the camera pushes in.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "POV: coming into work on Monday and remembering all of Fridays "Monday problems"". Audio: "oh f, oh my god"
why_it_went_viral: 131x median, 3.35 percent shares. "That's a Monday problem" is a phrase people in shops and on sites actually say on Friday, so seeing the bill come due is instantly recognized. A real person's face on a real site worked as well as a celebrity cutout.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Coworkers to each other on Monday morning, and to whoever said "Monday problem" on Friday
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Walk into the shop or up to the truck, look at something off camera and let the face drop, with a shop-phrase caption.

first_3_seconds: Kurt Angle cutout in a white tee stares wide-eyed and unblinking into the lens over a house construction photo. Nothing else moves.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "POV: a group of kids walks by the jobsite and you hear "that's us if we don't lock in fr""
why_it_went_viral: 104x median, 3.78 percent shares on 7 seconds. Self-deprecating pride: tradesmen being used as the cautionary tale and staring back. The audience laughs at the insult because they recognize it.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Tradesmen to the crew chat, and to younger family members as a joke
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Overheard insult as the text, his own blank stare into the lens as the whole video.

first_3_seconds: Steve Carell cutout in a cardigan laughs and waves his hands as if telling a story, over a construction site photo. Two blocks of text carry the whole joke.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "Hey why do you call the boss's son Rusty... that's not his name?" "Me: It stands for Rusty Rifle... he doesn't work, and he can't be fired"
why_it_went_viral: 81x median but only 0.84 percent shares, the weakest share rate of this account's top ten. It is a written joke (a pun on the boss's son) that you read once, not a feeling you recognize, and it risks landing on the wrong person if sent at work.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Workers at family-run shops to a trusted coworker, quietly
shape_jacob_can_borrow_alone: Question and answer nickname joke in two text blocks over his own laugh. Lower priority, puns share worse than feelings here.

first_3_seconds: A cutout of Hasbulla (an internet personality with dwarfism) sits in an excavator seat holding a phone up like he is filming himself.
spoken_or_text_hook: Text: "POV: Your not an operator so you snap everyone on your phone during the 5mins in the machine"
why_it_went_viral: avoid: the visual gag leans on a man with a growth disorder looking like a child in the operator seat. For reference only, it did 72x median at 1.61 percent shares.
who_shares_it_and_to_whom: Operators to the laborer who posts every time he touches a machine
